title: Infleqtion Opens Global Headquarters in Colorado and Announces 2027 Quantum Sensing Mineral Field Test - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Newly NYSE-listed neutral-atom developer Infleqtion (INFQ) opened its Colorado global HQ and announced a 2027 field test of Quantum Gravity Gradiometry to map critical mineral deposits, backed by pending federal legislation directing USGS to adopt quantum gravity sensors.

insights.claim: Neutral-atom quantum developer Infleqtion inaugurated the Colorado Quantum Innovation Center in Louisville, Colorado, as its new global headquarters, anchoring full-stack production of neutral-atom quantum processors alongside precision sensing hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Consolidating full-stack QPU and sensing production signals a scale-up from lab to manufacturing footprint.

insights.claim: The center operates in the Boulder-Louisville-Broomfield corridor alongside JILA, University of Colorado Boulder, NIST, and Elevate Quantum, the federally designated regional Tech Hub overseeing a consortium of over 100 quantum organizations across the Mountain West.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Co-location with national labs and a federal Tech Hub strengthens talent and research access for the company.

insights.claim: Infleqtion's dual-use portfolio at the new center includes optical atomic clocks, quantum radio frequency receivers, and ultra-cold atom inertial navigation units alongside its neutral-atom processors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A diversified sensing product line provides revenue paths beyond quantum computing hardware.

insights.claim: The headquarters opening follows Infleqtion's public listing on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker INFQ following its business combination with Churchill Capital Corp X.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A SPAC-route public listing gives Infleqtion capital-markets access to fund its manufacturing and sensing expansion.

insights.claim: Infleqtion announced a 2027 field demonstration of its Quantum Gravity Gradiometry technology to map subsurface critical mineral deposits across Colorado's Third Congressional District, measuring local variations in Earth's gravitational gradient to locate deposits before costly exploratory drilling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A concrete field application targets the strategically hot critical-minerals market as a near-term commercial use case.

insights.claim: The demonstration supports the Quantum-Enhanced Critical Minerals Mapping Act of 2026 (H.R. 9646), introduced by Rep. Jeff Hurd, which directs the USGS to integrate quantum gravity sensors into its Earth Mapping Resources Initiative, and Infleqtion CEO Matt Kinsella testified before the House Committee on Natural Resources in support.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Pending legislation could create a federal procurement channel for Infleqtion's gravity sensors if enacted.

insights.claim: Infleqtion is expanding its defense and civil sensing portfolio alongside existing programs with the U.S. Department of War, NASA, and the UK Royal Navy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Existing government deployments provide validation and recurring revenue anchors for the sensing business.
